note: Pre-registered phrase list for LIBRARIAN (collective agent module 3). A phrase is testable against a filing only if it was declared BEFORE that filing was published -- qt.librarian.check_declared_before refuses otherwise, and librarian_diff.py counts the refusals rather than skipping them quietly. Adding a phrase is free; it simply cannot be applied backwards. These phrases are canonical distress and disclosure language from auditing and reporting practice, deliberately NOT chosen by reading any particular company's filing.

phrases.why: The auditor's own doubt, in the auditor's own words. Its APPEARANCE is the loudest single phrase in a filing; its DISAPPEARANCE after a prior appearance is a resolution the market often prices slowly.
The statutory companion to going concern. Tested separately because the two are not always used together, and a filing can drop one while keeping the other.
An admitted failure of internal control. Removal usually means a remediation the company believes is complete -- a claim worth checking against the next restatement.
Prior numbers were wrong. Appearance is the event; persistence across quarters says the clean-up is not finished.
Lenders, not shareholders, set the binding constraint on a levered company. Language about covenants entering or leaving a filing tracks who is actually in control.
A covenant that needed forgiving. Tested separately from 'covenant' because the waiver is the breach made visible.
The exchange's patience is finite and its notices are disclosed. Directly adjacent to the abandoned specification 4, which found this signal unreachable from prices alone.
Most often a bid-price rescue rather than a capital decision. Appearance frequently precedes a delisting fight.
Management conceding that something it bought is worth less than it paid. A non-cash charge with cash-flow information in it.
A business being exited. Its arrival reshapes every margin comparison that follows, which is exactly when quarter-over-quarter reading goes wrong.
